neighbours.label: a military or armed security force named in a security/emergency context (Army, military, bomb squad, defense)
fire: When the shooting started, the townspeople heard the Army trucks rolling in.
Police officers and military units sealed off the roads around the airport.
After the threat, the county called in the bomb squad from the capital.
The governor deployed National Guard soldiers to patrol the flooded streets.
Members of the defense forces guarded the embassy throughout the night.
Witnesses said that Navy helicopters circled the harbor for an hour.
Troops from the Marine Corps arrived to secure the damaged bridge.
The ceremony was guarded by armed soldiers and special forces teams.
quiet: When the storm started, the townspeople heard the delivery trucks rolling in.
Volunteers and church groups handed out water around the airport.
After the flood, the county called in the repair crew from the capital.
The governor sent city workers to clear the flooded streets quickly.
Members of the hotel staff cleaned the embassy throughout the night.
Witnesses said that news helicopters circled the harbor for an hour.
Workers from the power company arrived to fix the damaged bridge lights.
The ceremony was attended by local teachers and their students.

notes: Card: ' Army' helicopters, State Police ' bomb' squad, ' defense' protective services, policiers et ' milit'aires; output + pole promotes police/cops, so - pole is the armed-force side. Near misses keep the emergency scene with civilian services.
